name: Rancid
label: Epitaph
lede: Tim Armstrong and Matt Freeman buried Operation Ivy at Gilman Street, started over sober, said no to Madonna's label, and ended up on MTV.

eras.title: After Operation Ivy, a sober start
eras.text: Two Albany kids who had played together since Little League watched Operation Ivy end at Gilman Street. Armstrong was drinking hard, and Livermore says he was hospitalized three times by 1992. Rancid was where he landed.

years.h: Operation Ivy plays its last show at 924 Gilman Street
years.p: Matt Freeman's verdict on the end of the Berkeley ska-punk band he played bass in with Tim Armstrong. Its only album was just coming out.
years.xp:
Operation Ivy formed in 1987 around the all-ages co-op at 924 Gilman Street: Armstrong on guitar, Freeman on bass, Jesse Michaels on vocals, Dave Mello on drums. Freeman told Larry Livermore the band got "a little more... too serious". Armstrong's version: "We decided we didn't want to do it anymore."

Armstrong was drinking heavily by then. He told Livermore he was "so annihilated I could barely put the chords together", and Livermore says Armstrong was hospitalized three times for alcohol and drugs between 1989 and 1992. Wikipedia's biography says he ended up homeless.

years.cap: Armstrong before a house party at the Pill Hill zoo house
years.h: Sober, Armstrong starts Rancid with his roommate on drums
years.p: Brett Reed takes the drum seat. Freeman, already in other bands, takes a year to commit, Armstrong says.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's biography says Freeman suggested a new band partly to help Armstrong stay sober. Armstrong's own telling to Livermore is slower: Freeman was playing with MDC and Gr'ups, and "it took me a year after the Salvation Army before Matt would commit to Rancid."

The trio began by jamming and played house parties and Gilman shows.

eras.title: A Berkeley EP, then Brett's label
eras.text: Rancid put out a first EP on Lookout!, moved to Brett Gurewitz's Epitaph, cut a debut with no ska on it, and found a second guitarist in a 19-year-old who had turned them down first.

years.h: First EP lands on Lookout!, Operation Ivy's old label
years.p: Rancid releases it a few months after forming, before moving to Epitaph.
years.xp: Lookout! was the Berkeley label run by Larry Livermore, home to Operation Ivy and Green Day. Rancid then moved to [[Brett Gurewitz|cd40188b-ea30-4729-bebb-e8c5091c9d02]]'s Epitaph.

years.h: Rancid's first album skips the ska and leans on the bass
years.p: Fifteen songs cut at Westbeach Recorders in Culver City with producer Donnell Cameron. Brett Gurewitz sings backup.
years.xp: Recorded from September 1992 to January 1993. AllMusic noted it has no ska at all, just heavy bass leads and Armstrong's slurred vocals. It was the first of three Rancid albums with the same title.

years.big: "Oh God, this is what I've been waiting for my whole life."
years.h: Lars Frederiksen says no, then yes
years.p: Armstrong asks the 19-year-old first. Frederiksen, on tour with the UK Subs, declines. Green Day's Billie Joe passes too, and Frederiksen reconsiders.
years.xp:
Frederiksen told Livermore what he felt hearing the band: "I put the record on first, and I went, oh God, this is what I've been waiting for my whole life."

Wikipedia puts him on Let's Go (1994), though the draft this page grew from dated his debut to the 1993 EP Radio Radio Radio.

eras.title: Madonna calls, Rancid stays put
eras.text: Green Day and the Offspring had just made punk a major-label business. Rancid turned the majors down, made ...And Out Come the Wolves, and got on MTV anyway.

years.cap: Ticket for Rancid and Voodoo Glow Skulls at La Luna, Portland, Sept 7, 1994
years.h: Let's Go starts as a double album and ends as one disc
years.p: Brett Gurewitz produces at Fantasy Studios in Berkeley, the first of his Rancid records: 23 songs in six days.
years.xp: Recording ran from October 1993 to March 1994. "Salvation" went to alternative radio in early 1995 and MTV picked up the video. The album peaked at 97 on the Billboard 200 and went gold in 2000.

years.h: Let's Go wins Outstanding Debut Album at the Bammies
years.p: The California Music Awards give it the prize. Rancid wins again in 1998, for Life Won't Wait.

q: We decided it would be dumb not to stay with Brett Gurewitz.
years.h: Madonna's label, Maverick, wants Rancid. Rancid says no
years.p: Tim Armstrong on Madonna: cool, but an international superstar. Rancid stays at Epitaph with Brett Gurewitz instead of signing with Maverick or Sony.
years.xp: After Green Day's Dookie and the Offspring's Smash, majors chased every punk band in the Bay Area. Armstrong's reasoning, to Livermore: "We decided it would be dumb not to stay with Brett Gurewitz, a real record guy, a punk rock record guy."

years.h: MTV discovers the East Bay with ...And Out Come the Wolves
years.p: Recorded at Fantasy in Berkeley and Electric Lady in New York, with Gurewitz stepping in when Jerry Finn's schedule fell through.
years.xp:
"Roots Radicals", "Time Bomb" and "Ruby Soho" all charted on Modern Rock Tracks and got heavy MTV rotation. The album peaked at 45 on the Billboard 200, went gold on January 22, 1996, and platinum in 2004. Wikipedia gives August 22 as the release date; the Grammy site says August 15.

"Journey to the End of the East Bay" tells the story of a young band's struggle, and "Daly City Train" is named for the BART line.

years.h: "Ruby Soho" climbs to 13 on Modern Rock Tracks
years.p: Often called the band's biggest song, it stays a concert staple alongside "Time Bomb".

eras.title: Kingston, Hellcat, and a Warner deal with no logo
eras.text: Rancid followed its ska and reggae roots to Jamaica, went back to hardcore, started Armstrong's own label, and took a Warner distribution deal that the packaging never mentions.

years.h: Hellcat Records starts as Armstrong's corner of Epitaph
years.p: Armstrong scouts the bands and has the final say on signings.
years.xp: Armstrong's Wikipedia biography dates Hellcat to 1997; the band's own article says 1999. The first Rancid album on Hellcat came in 2000.

years.h: Rancid cuts Life Won't Wait partly in Kingston
years.p: "Hoover Street" and the title track were recorded in Jamaica, with Buju Banton on the title song. Armstrong and Frederiksen produce.
years.xp:
Dr. Israel sings on "Coppers", and Dicky Barrett and Green Day's Billie Joe Armstrong add vocals. Gurewitz only helped with sequencing. Wikipedia says the mix of reggae, rockabilly, dub and hip-hop drew comparisons to the Clash's Sandinista!.

It peaked at 35 on the Billboard 200 and 32 in the UK, and won Outstanding Punk/Ska Album at the California Music Awards.

years.h: Back to hardcore: Rancid runs 22 songs in 38 minutes
years.p: The first record on Hellcat, cut in April 2000 at Westbeach and Sound City, answers the ska of Life Won't Wait with speed.
years.xp: Gurewitz returned as producer and stayed for the next five albums. "Let Me Go" was the lone official single, and Armstrong directed a joint video for "Don Giovanni" and "Disgruntled".

years.h: Armstrong, Rob Aston and Travis Barker start The Transplants
years.p: The side project puts out albums in 2002, 2005 and 2017.
years.xp: [[Tim Armstrong|beaecc2d-20c7-4221-8fd2-682c82f0faab]] also produced and wrote for artists from Jimmy Cliff to Pink.

years.h: Warner distributes Indestructible, and the logo stays off
years.p: The band keeps Warner's name off the packaging to reassure fans. The album debuts at 15 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp:
Wikipedia says the Warner link drew backlash from fans questioning Rancid's punk credentials; the album sold 51,000 copies its first week. A Warner spokesman called it "a unique deal that doesn't play by the traditional record biz rules".

Gurewitz produced across Los Angeles studios; the band cut 25 songs and used 19. Armstrong's divorce from Brody Dalle informed "Fall Back Down" and "Tropical London". Frederiksen dedicated the closer "Otherside" to his brother Robert, who died in 2001.

eras.title: Everybody scatters, then The Echo
eras.text: Armstrong had The Transplants, Frederiksen had the Bastards, Freeman went out with Social Distortion. In 2006 the band came back at a Los Angeles club, and lost its drummer by November.

years.h: Armstrong, Frederiksen and Freeman each head elsewhere
years.p: Armstrong tours with The Transplants, Frederiksen releases Viking with the Bastards, and Freeman goes out with Social Distortion.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists Haunted Cities (The Transplants, 2005) and Armstrong's solo A Poet's Life (2007) among the projects.

years.cap: Frederiksen and Armstrong on stage, August 17, 2006
years.h: Rancid plays The Echo again for Hellcat Nights
years.p: The band reforms in early 2006 after a two-year break, for acoustic shows at the Los Angeles club.

years.cap: Rancid at the Warfield, San Francisco, 2006
years.h: Brett Reed leaves after 15 years; Branden Steineckert of The Used takes over
years.p: Reed's last recording with the band was Indestructible, the only Rancid album with his songwriting.

eras.title: Still touring
eras.text: With Steineckert on drums, Rancid keeps making records, finally beats the chart mark Wolves set, and ends up on tour with Green Day.

years.cap: Armstrong at House of Blues, Boston, July 2009
years.h: Let the Dominoes Fall is Rancid's highest chart entry yet
years.p: Booker T. Jones plays organ on "Up to No Good". The album debuts at 11 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp: Recorded January 2008 to February 2009 with Gurewitz, it was Steineckert's first album with the band and Rancid's first in six years. It sold 33,000 copies its first week. European release was June 1, US June 2.

years.cap: Rancid on the main stage at West Coast Riot
years.h: Years of delays, then ...Honor Is All We Know
years.p: Work began in 2011 with Gurewitz. The album peaks at 15 on the Billboard 200.
years.xp: A 2012 release slipped, with recording done by March 2013. "Everybody's Sufferin'" covers Laurel Aitken, the band's first cover on a full-length since 1991.

years.h: Trouble Maker sells 18,000 in its first week
years.p: It debuts at 23 on the Billboard 200 and reaches number 2 on Top Alternative Albums.

years.h: Tomorrow Never Comes, album ten, lands at 126
years.p: It sells 9,500 copies in its first week, but makes the top 20 on the Rock and Alternative charts.

years.h: Rancid joins Green Day and The Smashing Pumpkins on the Saviors Tour
years.p: The North American run puts the two East Bay bands on the same bill again.
